adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — [P1; confidence 100] `String getShortcut();` adds an abstract method to the provider SPI, so an already-compiled custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` throws `AbstractMethodError` during `postInit` when the server calls `gtf.getShortcut()` and prevents startup.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut()` to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface (line 33). This is a breaking change for any existing third-party implementations of this interface. When the server starts and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` iterates over all `OAuth2GrantType` provider factories and calls `gtf.getShortcut()`, any pre-compiled custom implementation that doesn't have this method will throw `AbstractMethodError`. The diff shows this exact call pattern in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java` lines 68-73 where it calls `gtf.getShortcut()` on each factory. This is a real binary compatibility issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74 — [P1; confidence 100] `if (encodedContext.length() != 6)` rejects every token produced by a grant factory using the documented three-letter shortcut, so the advertised encode/decode framework cannot recover context for those custom grants.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that 3-letter shortcuts would fail the length check, but examining the diff shows that all grant shortcuts defined are exactly 2 characters (e.g., 'ac', 'cc', 'rt', 'pg', 'pc', 'ro', 'te', 'ci', 'dg'). The Javadoc comment in OAuth2GrantTypeFactory says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut' but this is just documentation guidance, not a requirement. The actual implementation uses 2-character shortcuts consistently. The encoded context format is: 2 chars (sessionType) + 2 chars (tokenType) + 2 chars (grantType) = 6 chars total, which matches the length check. The finding misreads the code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:113 — [P1; confidence 75] `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType);` overwrites the mapping for an existing shortcut when a newly deployed grant collides, causing previously issued token IDs to decode as the new grant type instead of the grant that minted them.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in getGrantTypeByShortcut() at line 113, when a new grant type is deployed with a shortcut that already exists in grantsByShortcuts, the code will overwrite the existing mapping with `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, newGrantType)`. This means if two different grant types have the same shortcut (which the postInit validation only catches at startup, not for dynamically deployed grants), tokens minted with the original grant type would decode as the new grant type. However, looking more carefully at the code flow: the method is called when decoding a token ID that contains a shortcut not found in the map. If the shortcut already exists in the map, this code path wouldn't be reached. The issue would only occur if a new grant is deployed with a duplicate shortcut - the postInit validation would catch this at startup but not for hot-deployed grants. This is a real edge case bug for dynamic grant deployment scenarios.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/test/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java:49 — [P2; confidence 75] `provider = new DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider(null, factory);` leaves the new `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` production path entirely unexercised, so regressions in session type, lightweight-token, or absent-grant context encoding ship without a test failure.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test file creates DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider with a null session parameter and manually configured factory maps, which means getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext() is never tested (calling it would cause NPE due to null session). The diff shows this method contains significant new logic for determining session type, token type, and grant type from ClientSessionContext. While the test covers getTokenContextFromTokenId() and encodeTokenId() thoroughly, the production path through getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext() (called from TokenManager.initToken) has no unit test coverage. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added nontrivial logic.
